original_question: For commuting transformations T1, ..., Tℓ and bounded functions f0, ..., fℓ, does every correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ dµ admit a decomposition ψ(n) + e(n) where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro average of |e(n)| tends to 0?
target_in_paper: Section 5.2.6, Problem 20 (Optimal error term for decomposition results) in the 2016 version of arXiv:1103.3808; this is the sharpened one-parameter decomposition problem for commuting transformations, not the broader multivariable structural question from Section 4.1, Problem 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very accurately: the sequence is the one-parameter multiple correlation sequence n ↦ ∫ f0·T1^n f1·...·Tℓ^n fℓ dμ, the transformations commute, the functions are bounded, the desired structured term is an ℓ-step nilsequence, and the error term is required to satisfy the Cesàro-null condition (1/N)Σ_{n=1}^N |e(n)| → 0. This is much closer to Section 5.2.6, Problem 20 than to the broader Section 4.1 questions. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient object is a system (X, 𝓧, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ), where μ is a probability measure and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations acting on the same space; that is implicit in your draft but not stated. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The functions are not just bounded abstractly; they are bounded measurable functions f0, ..., fℓ in L∞(μ). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The quantifiers should be explicit: for every ℓ ∈ ℕ, every such system, and every choice of f0, ..., fℓ, does there exist a decomposition of the associated sequence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The operator notation should be spelled out in a stand-alone formulation: T_i^n f_i means f_i ∘ T_i^n. This is standard in the paper’s framework but unstated in the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The index set should be made explicit: the sequence is a one-variable sequence indexed by n ∈ ℕ (the paper formulates the Cesàro condition via averages from 1 to N). ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Nilsequence should be defined if the question is to be fully stand-alone: in Section 2.4.2 an ℓ-step nilsequence is a uniform limit of basic sequences n ↦ F(g^n x) on an ℓ-step nilmanifold G/Γ, with F continuous. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The paper explicitly emphasizes that no ergodicity assumption is being made; your draft leaves this hidden. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To stay maximally paper-faithful, the notation N(n)+e(n) used in the paper is preferable to ψ(n)+e(n), although mathematically your notation is harmless. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let ℓ ∈ ℕ and let (X, 𝓧, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) be a measure-preserving system, meaning that μ is a probability measure and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of X. For arbitrary f0, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(μ), define the one-parameter multiple correlation sequence a(n) by a(n) = ∫ f0·(f1∘T1^n)·...·(fℓ∘Tℓ^n) dμ for n ∈ ℕ. Is it always possible, without any ergodicity assumption, to decompose a(n) as a(n) = N(n) + e(n), where (N(n)) is a one-variable ℓ-step nilsequence (that is, a uniform limit of basic sequences n ↦ F(g^n x) on ℓ-step nilmanifolds G/Γ) and lim_{N→∞} (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N |e(n)| = 0? ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is aiming at the later sharpened decomposition problem in Section 5.2.6, not at the broader structural Problem 1 from Section 4.1. Section 5.2.6 first recalls a previously proved decomposition result for multiple correlation sequences defined by commuting transformations and then asks whether one always has exactly the decomposition ∫ f0·T1^n f1·...·Tℓ^n fℓ dμ = N(n)+e(n), with N an ℓ-step nilsequence and Cesàro-null error; this matches your draft almost verbatim. Section 1.2 supplies the standing framework for systems and transformations, and Section 2.4.2 supplies the definition of nilsequence that must be imported if the question is to be stand-alone. The main omissions in the draft are therefore not mathematical direction but hidden hypotheses: invertibility and measure-preservation of the T_i, the common probability space, the L∞(μ) status of the f_i, the one-variable nature of the sequence, and the explicit absence of any ergodicity assumption. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
